items: Caches the preflight result, skipping the round trip
Cache key = (origin, URL, method, header set)
A different method or header set re-preflights
`Max-Age: 0` disables it — use while debugging

blocks.title: Missing OPTIONS In Logs
blocks.text: Preflights appear once per cache window. A silent log does not mean the probe never happened — it may just be cached.

items: Required whenever ACAO depends on the request `Origin`
CDNs and reverse proxies key their cache on `Vary`
Without it, one cached ACAO is served to everyone
A static `ACAO: *` needs no `Vary` — origin-independent

blocks.title: Poisoning, Both Ways
items: Attacker origin cached, app blocked
Or app origin cached, leak widened
Same missing header causes both
`Vary: Origin` fixes both
Add `Vary: Access-Control-Request-Headers`
And `Vary: Access-Control-Request-Method`
Needed when the answer varies by them
Otherwise one probe's answer serves a different shape
Keep endpoints simple-request-shaped where possible
Or raise `Max-Age`, or consolidate custom headers
Preflight cache is per-browser-profile
Hard reload with 'Disable cache' clears it

blocks.text: Measure it: on a 100ms RTT link a preflighted call costs ~200ms before the first byte of real work.

blocks.title: Cached Config Regression
blocks.text: A cached preflight can mask a server-side CORS regression for hours after a deploy. High Max-Age slows propagation of every fix.

items: `no-cors` is not a bypass — the body stays unreadable
Useful only for fire-and-forget or cache warming
Opaque responses still eat cache storage quota
And they are padded, so at an inflated size
Every hop in the chain must pass CORS
Cross-origin redirect can reset the origin to `null`
`redirect: 'manual'` yields an opaque-redirect response
`redirect: 'error'` fails fast — good for diagnosis
CORS does not stop a request from executing
State-changing routes need SameSite + anti-CSRF tokens
JSONP was the pre-CORS `<script>` callback hack
No method control, no header control, runs attacker JS

blocks.title: JSONP Is Dead
blocks.text: It executes third-party JS in your page with zero controls. Never revive it, not even for one legacy endpoint.

items: CORP values: `same-origin | same-site | cross-origin`

`Timing-Allow-Origin` gates Resource Timing detail

blocks.title: WebSockets Opt Out
blocks.text: WebSockets do not use CORS at all. The server must read and validate the `Origin` header itself during the handshake.

blocks.text: `CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS = True` combined with credentials. It is the reflect-any-origin bug shipped as a config flag.

This 10-part field guide walks the whole CORS handshake — origin triples, the simple-request safelist, the OPTIONS probe, the credentials wildcard ban, Vary and cache poisoning, and the reflection bug that hands your authenticated JSON to any site on the internet.
